extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users creating graphics with TikZ (drawing automata, calendars, backgrounds, and arrow tips)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference/documentation for using TikZ library features (arrows, automata, backgrounds, calendar). Describes options, styles, and recommended steps for producing these diagram types.

rubrics_metrics.name: rotate around option
rubrics_metrics.description: rotate around={angle:(coordinate)} rotates the coordinate system by angle degrees around the specified point (coordinate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw[rotate around={40:(1,1)}] ... rotates by 40° around (1,1). Also shown: negative angles (e.g., -20). Use to apply rotation to drawn paths within the current scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: cm option (coordinate transformation matrix)
rubrics_metrics.description: cm={a,b,c,d,(tx,ty)} applies the affine transformation given by the 2×2 matrix [a b; c d] and translation (tx,ty) to all coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transforms each coordinate (x,y) via matrix multiplication plus translation; usually not used directly by casual users. Examples show cm={1,1,0,1,(0,0)} and cm={0,1,1,0,(1cm,1cm)}.

rubrics_metrics.name: reset cm
rubrics_metrics.description: reset cm completely resets the coordinate transformation matrix to the identity matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: This destroys transformations applied in the current scope and all inherited transformations from surrounding scopes. Do not use unless you understand consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: triangular arrow tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Predefined triangular arrow tip shapes available (e.g., latex', stealth', triangle 90/60/45 and their 'reversed' variants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each name yields thick and thin variants. Use \usetikzlibrary{arrows} or \usetikzlibrary{arrows} and pick tip names when setting arrow heads in paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: barbed arrow tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Predefined barbed arrow tips (angle 90/60/45, hooks and their reversed variants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each yields thick and thin variants; choose appropriate angle or hook style to represent barbed arrow heads.

rubrics_metrics.name: bracket-like arrow tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Bracket-like arrow tips are provided ([-], ]-[, (-), )-( ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each yields thick and thin variants. Use these for bracket-shaped terminations on lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: circle and diamond arrow tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrow tips providing circle/diamond shapes (o, *, diamond, open diamond).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each yields thick and thin variants. Useful for endpoints, markers or diamond-shaped tips on edges.

rubrics_metrics.name: serif-like arrow tips
rubrics_metrics.description: serif cm arrow tip style (serif-like).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yields thick and thin variants; provided for serif-style line endings.

rubrics_metrics.name: partial arrow tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial arrow tips such as left to, right to, left/right hook and their reversed variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provide specialized partial-tip shapes that only occupy one side; each yields thick and thin variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: line caps
rubrics_metrics.description: Predefined line cap shapes (round cap, butt cap, triangle 90 cap, fast cap and reversed variants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yields specific appearance for path ends. Documentation lists results for a line width of 1ex; pick cap matching visual needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: automata drawing: one-node-per-state
rubrics_metrics.description: For each automaton state, create one node with the option state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the foundational rule for drawing automata: each state must correspond to a distinct node with the state style.

rubrics_metrics.name: automata drawing: placement of states
rubrics_metrics.description: Place states using absolute or relative positions (options like above of or right of).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relative placement (node distance and anchors) simplifies layout; absolute positions can be used for precise control.

rubrics_metrics.name: automata drawing: unique node names
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a unique name to each state node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming nodes allows later referencing in \path/\draw commands and for connecting edges unambiguously.

rubrics_metrics.name: automata drawing: marking initial/accepting states
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate accepting and initial states by adding the options accepting and initial to state nodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The styles accepting and initial select how these nodes are rendered (double circle, arrow, etc.). See accepting/initial style options for customization.

rubrics_metrics.name: automata drawing: adding edges
rubrics_metrics.description: Once states are placed, add edges using the edge operation (or by drawing after node placement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The edge operation is most useful; use edge [loop] for self-loops. Use node labels on edges to show transition symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: automata drawing: loop edges
rubrics_metrics.description: For loops, use the edge [loop] operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify loop location (e.g., loop above, loop below) and label with node {...} to show transition symbols on the loop.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=state without output
rubrics_metrics.description: Node style that draws nodes as simple circles and calls every state styling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when states do not have output fields; this is the default underlying style for plain states.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=state with output
rubrics_metrics.description: Node style that draws nodes as split circles (circle split shape) with top for name and lower part for output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify output using \nodepart{lower} inside the node. This style also invokes every state style.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=state (redefinition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The style=state is set to state without output by default, but you can redefine it to another state style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \tikzstyle{state}=[state with output] so that \node[state] will produce split-circle states.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every state
rubrics_metrics.description: Style executed by both state with output and state without output; default does nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use it to apply uniform styling to all states (e.g., color, fill, line thickness). Example: \tikzstyle{every state}=[draw=blue!50,very thick,fill=blue!20].

rubrics_metrics.name: style=initial and initial by arrow options
rubrics_metrics.description: style=initial selects initial state rendering; initial by arrow adds an arrow and optional text pointing to the node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: initial text=(text) (default 'start', empty to suppress text), initial where=(above|below|left|right), initial distance=(distance) sets arrow length. Use style=initial above/below/left/right for shorthand variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every initial by arrow
rubrics_metrics.description: Style executed at the beginning of every path that contains the initial arrow and text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to customize the appearance of the initial arrow/text globally (e.g., make it red). Accumulates at path start.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=accepting and accepting variants
rubrics_metrics.description: style=accepting selects how accepting states are rendered; accepting by double (double circle) and accepting by arrow (arrow & text) are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: accepting text=(text) (default text shown, empty to suppress), accepting where=(above|below|left|right), accepting by double draws double line, accepting by arrow points an arrow from node to the text. Default accepting selects accepting by double.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every accepting by arrow and shorthands
rubrics_metrics.description: Style executed at the beginning of every path that contains the accepting arrow and text; accepting above/below/left/right are shorthands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to apply consistent appearance for accepting-by-arrow constructions; e.g., color or text style.

rubrics_metrics.name: background: style=show background rectangle
rubrics_metrics.description: Draws a rectangle behind the graphic when given to the {tikzpicture} or \tikz command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rectangle size is the picture's bounding box plus inner frame separations. Use to create framed pictures or coloured backdrop.

rubrics_metrics.name: background: inner frame xsep/ ysep / sep
rubrics_metrics.description: inner frame xsep sets horizontal extra separator (default 1ex); inner frame ysep sets vertical; inner frame sep sets both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls padding between bounding box and background rectangle. Use tight background (0pt) or loose background (2ex) as convenient shorthands.

rubrics_metrics.name: background: style=background rectangle
rubrics_metrics.description: Dictates how the background rectangle path is drawn or filled (default draw).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can set draw/fill/colors/rounded corners/double lines/top color etc. Examples show fancy combinations, but typical use is fill=blue!20 or draw=blue!50.

rubrics_metrics.name: background: style=framed shorthand
rubrics_metrics.description: framed is a shorthand for show background rectangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use framed for brevity when you want the framed background rectangle.

rubrics_metrics.name: background: show background grid and background grid style
rubrics_metrics.description: show background grid draws a grid behind the picture (computed like the background rectangle); background grid style defines its appearance (default draw,help lines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customize step size and drawing style, e.g., \tikzstyle{background grid}=[thick,draw=red,step=.5cm]. Use gridded as shorthand for show background grid. Can combine framed and gridded.

rubrics_metrics.name: background: show background top/bottom/left/right and outer frame sep options
rubrics_metrics.description: show background top (and bottom/left/right) draws only the corresponding line of the background rectangle; outer frame xsep/ysep/sep add extra length to these lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use outer frame xsep to lengthen top line; combine with background rectangle style to control line width/color. background top style (default draw) controls drawing attributes for the top line.

rubrics_metrics.name: \calendar command: syntax elements
rubrics_metrics.description: \calendar calendar_specification; is only available inside {tikzpicture}. The calendar specification is a sequence of elements: [options], ((name)), at ((coordinate)), and if ((date condition)) ... else ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the calendar-specific parser recognizes these elements. [options] can be any TikZ options applying to the whole calendar. The ((name)) element acts like name=name and allows later referencing of day nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every calendar
rubrics_metrics.description: Style applied at the beginning of every calendar; empty by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for calendar-global configuration when you cannot pass individual if conditionals inside the specification easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: dates option (date range)
rubrics_metrics.description: dates=start_date to end_date sets the date range the \calendar iterates over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates accept ISO-format (YYYY-MM-DD), 'last' for last day of month (e.g., 2006-02-last), and offsets via +-. Example: dates=2000-01-01 to 2000-01-31.

rubrics_metrics.name: day xshift / day yshift / month xshift / month yshift
rubrics_metrics.description: day xshift and day yshift set horizontal/vertical shifts between days (anchors of nodes); month xshift/month yshift set additional shifts between different months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults: day xshift 3.5ex, day yshift 3ex. These control spacing/grid of the calendar; month shifts space months relative to each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: at option (positioning the calendar) and placement strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: The calendar anchor of the first day is normally at the origin; use at={(x,y)} to move it. Alternatives: wrap calendar in a node or place inside a single-cell matrix to control specific anchors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matrix-based anchoring (anchor=cal-YYYY-MM-DD.center) gives clean positioning but may be less portable (e.g., SVG backend issues). Wrapping in a node allows normal anchor-based placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: day code
rubrics_metrics.description: day code={code} changes the code executed for each day. Default: \node[name=\pgfcalendarsuggestedname,every day]{\tikzdaytext};
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use day code to draw custom shapes for days (e.g., \fill[blue] (0,0) circle (2pt);). The default creates named nodes so individual days can be referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: default naming of day nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the calendar has a name, day nodes are named name-YYYY-MM-DD (ISO date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows referencing specific day nodes later (e.g., \draw[red] (mycal-2000-01-20) circle (4pt);). The naming arises from the default day code.

rubrics_metrics.name: day text and \% (pgfcalendarshorthand)
rubrics_metrics.description: day text=text changes \tikzdaytext; inside calendar, \% is redefined to \pgfcalendarshorthand and inserts pieces like day/month/year/day-of-week with format codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: first letter d/m/y/w selects type; second character selects display (- numeric, = numeric with leading space, 0 numeric with leading zero, t textual, . textual abbreviated). Example: day text=\%d0 yields 01 02 ... for single-digit days.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every day
rubrics_metrics.description: Style executed by the default node code for each day; default anchor=base east.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to change all day nodes' appearance (color, anchor). Example: \tikzstyle{every day}+=[red] to make day labels red; changing anchor to mid can affect alignment and may require adjusting day text spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: month/year labels: month code / month text / style=every month / year equivalents
rubrics_metrics.description: month code sets \tikzmonthcode, month text sets \tikzmonthtext, and style=every month customizes month labels. Similar options exist for years: year code/text and style=every year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default, month code nodes show textual month. Use month label styles (e.g., month label above centered) to display month labels. month text can include \% shorthands and formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: date ifs and if= option (conditionals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditionals allow executing code/options for dates matching specified tests. They can be put inline (if (conditions) {code} else {elsecode}) or via if=((conditions))(code) option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tests are evaluated by \ifdate / \pgfcalendarifdate; common tests include Monday, workday, weekend, equals, at least. If the condition matches, the code or options are applied for that date. Examples: if (Sunday) [red]; if (equals=2000-01-20) {\draw (0,0) circle (8pt);}.

rubrics_metrics.name: date-ifs: code vs options behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: If the date-if's branch is code (braced), the code is executed for that date; if it is a list of options (bracketed), those options are applied in a scope around the current date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction allows either drawing custom graphics on a date or simply changing drawing attributes for that date. Multiple date-ifs can be provided; they are not nested in the simple inline form.

rubrics_metrics.name: anchor and alignment considerations for day decorations
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual offsets may occur because date labels use anchors like base east; when drawing shapes centered on the date, adjust anchor (via style=every day) or day text to correct alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: change \tikzstyle{every day}=[anchor=mid] and use day text=\%d= to align single-digit days; otherwise decorations (like a circle) may appear offset relative to the visible label.

rubrics_metrics.name: current date code structure
rubrics_metrics.description: For each date the current date code executes in this order: before-scope code; open a scope; at-begin-scope code; execute all date-ifs; at-end-scope code; close scope; after-scope code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The separation of these pieces allows some code to affect following days (before/after scope) while other code is confined to the day's scope (at-begin/at-end). This enables different calendar arrangements (lists, grids, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: execute before/at-begin/at-end/after day scope options
rubrics_metrics.description: execute before day scope={code} runs before everything for each date; execute at begin day scope={code} runs inside the day's scope before rendering; execute at end day scope={code} runs just before closing the scope (accumulates in reverse); execute after day scope={code} runs after the day scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple uses accumulate (before and at-begin accumulate in order; at-end and after accumulate in reverse). Use these hooks to pair constructs (e.g., \scope and \endscope) or to compute positions and transformations that should or should not affect subsequent days.
